facts.statement: The genus Paleopsilopterus was described by Alvarenga in 1985.
Paleopsilopterus was a large, flightless, predatory bird.
facts.quote: Paleopsilopterus is an extinct genus of large, flightless, predatory birds

facts.statement: Paleopsilopterus belongs to the order Cariamiformes.
The genus is generally placed in the subfamily Psilopterinae and the family Phorusrhacidae.
facts.quote: It is generally placed in the subfamily Psilopterinae of the family Phorusrhacidae

facts.statement: The precise taxonomic placement of Paleopsilopterus remains debated.
facts.quote: although its precise taxonomic placement has been subject to debate

facts.statement: The animal lived specifically within the Itaboraian South American Land Mammal Age.
facts.quote: specifically within the Itaboraian South American Land Mammal Age

facts.statement: Fossils of the only known species, P. itaboraiensis, were found in the Itaboraí Formation near São José de Itaborai, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
facts.quote: Fossils of the only known species, Paleopsilopterus itaboraiensis, have been discovered in the Itaboraí Formation near São José de Itaborai in the state of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil

facts.statement: The time range for the genus is the Ypresian stage, from 56 to 48.07 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Ypresian to Ypresian (56 to 48.07 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Paleopsilopterus lived during the Early Eocene, approximately 53 to 50 million years ago.
rejected.quote: Paleopsilopterus lived during the Early Eocene (approximately 53 to 50 million years ago)
